fact: Ivorian customs says SYDAM World moved in 2014 to version 2, based on ASYCUDA World, with electronic payment, data exchange and interoperability services.

GUCE CI's terms of use say its e-DAU module lets customs agents enter and submit detailed customs declarations through the GUCE platform, partially used since 2016 because operators may also lodge declarations directly with SYDAM.

GUCE CI's terms of use describe GUCE as a transactional single-window web portal where operators meet import, export and transit formalities, with customs clearance modules (e-DAU, e-Risk) alongside technical-ministry pre-clearance modules.

ECOWAS says it launched deployment of SIGMAT between Cote d'Ivoire, Guinea and Liberia on 31 October 2025, exchanging electronic transit messages through interconnection of their national customs systems; Liberia joins Guinea and Cote d'Ivoire on the platform.
Ivorian customs describes its Douane Intelligente modernisation project, backed by Huawei, as being deployed, with a 5-14 December 2025 training mission to China.

The ECOWAS Commission says SIGMAT, its interconnected transit-goods system for electronic data exchange between Member States, has been in use by implementing states since 2019, and that a 21-25 July 2025 mission to Ghana resolved the technical and functional challenges hindering transit between Cote d'Ivoire and Ghana.

The Ministry of Commerce says the GUCE-CI single window lets traders complete import, export and transit formalities entirely online and is the central digital interface between operators, public administrations and banks, with ten years of service.
GUCE CI's director says traders have for several years submitted customs declarations and paid duties and taxes electronically through the GUCE transaction portal.
GUCE CI, the foreign-trade single window implemented in 2013, lets traders file customs formalities, licences and declarations electronically for the administrations involved.

Douanes Ivoiriennes report that Cote d Ivoire and Mali teams met on 24-25 September 2026 to assess SIGMAT in its operating phase on the Abidjan-Bamako transit corridor, sharing information between the two administrations.
ECOWAS says Cote d'Ivoire was connected to the SIGMAT goods-in-transit data exchange system for its customs administration in July 2024.
